Start working on Linear ticket [ENG-2312: Release mobile-supported DG obsidian](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2312/release-mobile-supported-dg-obsidian) by fetching its details and creating a dedicated git worktree.

## Steps

### 1. Validate input
- `[ENG-2312: Release mobile-supported DG obsidian](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2312/release-mobile-supported-dg-obsidian)` should be a Linear ticket ID like `ENG-1271`. If missing or malformed, ask the user.

### 2. Fetch ticket details from Linear
- Use `mcp__linear-server__get_issue` with the issue ID `[ENG-2312: Release mobile-supported DG obsidian](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2312/release-mobile-supported-dg-obsidian)`
- Extract: title, description, and `branchName` (Linear provides this)
- If the Linear tool is unavailable, ask the user for a branch name manually

### 3. Determine branch name
- Use the `branchName` field from Linear if available (it's already formatted correctly)
- Otherwise derive it: lowercase the ticket ID + hyphenated slug of the title
  - Example: `ENG-1271 Implement filter search` → `eng-1271-implement-filter-search`
  - Strip special characters, replace spaces with hyphens, truncate to ~60 chars

### 4. Create git worktree
Run these from the repo root (the main working directory, not an existing worktree):

```bash
# Fetch latest main so the worktree starts from up-to-date origin/main
git fetch origin main

# Check if branch already exists
git branch --list <branch-name>

# Check if worktree already exists
git worktree list | grep <branch-name>
```

- **If worktree already exists**: skip to step 5, just `cd` into `.claude/worktrees/<branch-name>`
- **If branch does NOT exist**: `git worktree add -b <branch-name> .claude/worktrees/<branch-name> origin/main`
- **If branch already exists but no worktree**: reset the branch to `origin/main` first, then add the worktree:
  ```bash
  git branch -f <branch-name> origin/main
  git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<branch-name> <branch-name>
  ```

### 5. Enter the worktree
**Do NOT use the `EnterWorktree` tool** — it always creates a brand-new worktree and will duplicate the one you just created.

Instead, use `cd` to switch into the worktree directory:
```bash
cd .claude/worktrees/<branch-name>
```

All subsequent commands should run from this path.

### 6. Install dependencies and set up the worktree
After entering the worktree, run the following to bootstrap the environment:

```bash
pnpm install
```

This is required because worktrees share git objects but each needs its own `node_modules`.

### 6b. Copy .env files from the main repo into the worktree
`.env` files are gitignored, so each worktree needs its own copies. After `pnpm install`, copy all `.env` files (excluding `.env.example` files) from the main repo root into the matching relative paths in the worktree.

The main repo root is the working directory you were in before entering the worktree (e.g. `/Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph`).

Run:
```bash
# From the main repo root, find all .env files (not .env.example) and copy them into the worktree
find . -name ".env*" \
  -not -name ".env.example" \
  -not -path "./.git/*" \
  -not -path "./node_modules/*" \
  -not -path "./.claude/worktrees/*" \
  | while read f; do
      dest=".claude/worktrees/<branch-name>/$f"
      mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
      cp "$f" "$dest"
    done
```

Report which files were copied so the user can confirm.

### 6c. Link the shared `dg-*` skills into the worktree

Claude Code only loads skills from `.claude/skills`, but the repo's shared skills live in
`.agents/skills`. Without this step they never load in the worktree: they cannot trigger on
their own descriptions and have no slash command.

Run from the main repo root, substituting the worktree path:

```bash
WT=".claude/worktrees/<branch-name>"
MAIN="$PWD"
mkdir -p "$WT/.claude/skills"
for src in "$MAIN"/.agents/skills/dg-*/; do
  s=$(basename "$src")
  if [ -d "$WT/.agents/skills/$s" ]; then
    # Relative link, so the worktree uses its own branch's copy of the skill.
    ln -sfn "../../.agents/skills/$s" "$WT/.claude/skills/$s"
  else
    # Branch predates the skill; fall back to the main checkout's copy.
    ln -sfn "$MAIN/.agents/skills/$s" "$WT/.claude/skills/$s"
  fi
done
ls -l "$WT/.claude/skills/"
```

Verify each link resolves before moving on:

```bash
for d in "$WT"/.claude/skills/dg-*; do
  [ -f "$d/SKILL.md" ] || echo "BROKEN: $d"
done
```

These links are gitignored (`.claude/*`), so they are local to this machine and add nothing
to the diff. Use a glob rather than a variable list: zsh does not word-split unquoted
variables, so `for s in $SKILLS` silently iterates once with the whole string.

### 7. Ask the user which app to start
Ask the user which app they want to run in dev mode. Common options:
- **Roam**: `SUPABASE_USE_DB=none pnpm -C <worktree>/apps/roam dev`
- **Obsidian**: `SUPABASE_USE_DB=local pnpm -C <worktree>/apps/obsidian dev`
- **None**: just set up the environment without starting a dev server

If the user says Roam, also switch the Roam dev symlink:
```bash
ln -sfn <worktree>/apps/roam/dist ~/roam-ext-dev
```
and remind them to reload the developer extension in Roam.

Run the chosen dev command in the background so the user can continue working.

**Dev server gotchas** (learned the hard way — don't rediscover these):

- The filter flag is `--filter`, not `--F`. Turbo 2.5.6 rejects `--F=roam` outright.
- Prefer `pnpm -C <abs-path> <app> dev` over `turbo dev --filter=<app>`. `turbo dev --filter=roam`
  also runs the `@repo/database#dev` dependency, which requires Docker Desktop plus an explicit
  `SUPABASE_USE_DB`; if Docker isn't running turbo fails the *entire* run even though the app
  itself built fine. Going through `pnpm -C` skips the dependency graph.
- `SUPABASE_USE_DB` must be one of `local | branch | production | none | implicit`
  (see `packages/database/src/dbDotEnv.mjs`). Use `none` for work that doesn't touch the database.
- **Always bake the absolute worktree path into the command.** The Bash tool's cwd resets to the
  main repo between calls, so a backgrounded `pnpm --filter roam dev` with no path silently builds
  the *main repo's* `dist` — not the worktree the symlink points at. `pnpm -C <abs-path>` makes the
  path intrinsic to the command so it can't be dropped.
- After starting, verify before reporting success: confirm the log says `built with 0 errors` **and**
  that `<worktree>/apps/roam/dist` has a fresh mtime. A background task that failed still returns a
  task ID.

### 8. Ingest any saved session context
The branch may have been worked on before (e.g. reset from an existing branch).
Check for recorded session context:

```bash
bash ~/.claude/scripts/session-context.sh resolve
```

- If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=yes`, **read the `CONTEXT_FILE`** and load it as working context
  (`Next step`, `Open questions`, `Key decisions`, `Dead ends`).
- If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=no` or the command errors, continue — this is a fresh start.

### 9. Show context
After setup, display:
- Ticket ID and title
- Branch name you're on
- Brief description from the ticket (if available)
- Which app dev server is running (if any)
- That the shared `dg-*` skills are linked and resolving
- If prior session context was found: its `TL;DR` and `Next step`
- A short "ready to work" confirmation
- Remind the user they can run `/checkpoint` to save session context before wrapping up

```ts
const FRONTMATTER_BLOCK =
```

## Keeping `nativeJsonFileDialogs.ts` costs nothing — tested

I removed `"electron"` from the esbuild externals and rebuilt with the file still in place:

- **`built with 0 errors`**
- The bundle contains exactly one hit, at `dist/main.js:48012`:

- Zero bare top-level `require("electron")`.

That's the whole answer: it's a **method call on the `window` object**, not an import. esbuild has nothing to resolve, so it passes it straight through regardless of the externals list. Same for `window.require("fs/promises")`. The file is inert at load time on mobile and only throws if someone actually invokes an export.

So: **keep it.** My earlier plan said "delete it" because that's what PR #1391 did — but that PR deleted it when it had zero importers, which was free. Today it has two, and deleting it would be pointless work for no mobile benefit.

## A picker that works on both

Split it by direction, because the two halves have very different answers:

**Reading (import) — genuinely unified, one code path, no `Platform` branch:**
```ts
const input = createEl("input", { attr: { type: "file", accept: "application/json" } });
input.onchange = async () => { const text = await input.files?.[0]?.text(); /* ... */ };
input.click();
```
`<input type="file">` works in Electron **and** in iOS/Android webviews — on mobile it opens the native Files/Photos picker. This is strictly better than the Electron open dialog, and it's free: `openJsonFromUserLocation` is **dead code** with no call sites, so there's nothing to migrate. Whenever schema import lands, build it this way.

**Writing (export) — cannot be truly unified, and the reason is the OS, not our code.** Mobile apps are sandboxed; there is no "save to an arbitrary location" on iOS/Android. `<a download>` + Blob works in Electron but is unreliable-to-blocked in WKWebView. So the options are:

| Option | Desktop | Mobile | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Vault write everywhere** — `vault.create(path, json)` + `Notice` | Works | Works | One path, testable, deletes the last Electron code. Loses "save outside the vault" |
| **B. Branch on `Platform.isDesktopApp`** — native dialog on desktop, vault write on mobile | Unchanged | Works | Keeps the file; two paths to maintain |
| **C. Leave as-is** | Unchanged | Shows "requires Obsidian desktop" `Notice` | Zero work |

I'd go **A** if saving outside the vault isn't a real user need, **B** if it is. `ExportSpecsModal` already catches and surfaces the error, so **C** ships today without breaking anything.

One thing I won't claim without a device: `navigator.share()` would be the nice mobile export, but I can't verify it works in Obsidian's `capacitor://` context from here.

## `mime-types` done — and your instinct caught a real bug

The naive port from PR #1391 **would have broken desktop asset sync.** Differential-testing the PR's curated table against the real `mime-types` package found:

| Extension | PR #1391 table | Real `mime-types` | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.xml` | `text/xml` → **skipped** | `application/xml` → uploaded | **XML assets silently stop uploading** |
| `.flac` | `audio/flac` | `audio/x-flac` | Wrong `contentType` stored (Obsidian-accepted audio) |
| `.3gp` | *(missing)* → `octet-stream` | `video/3gpp` | Wrong `contentType` (Obsidian-accepted audio) |
| `.canvas` | `application/json` | `octet-stream` | Changed stored type |
| 92 more | *(missing)* → `octet-stream` | `text/*` → skipped | **Files that were skipped start uploading** — including `.markdown`, `.mdx`, `.htm`, `.tsv`, `.log` |

That last row is the nastiest: `findEmbeddedAttachments` reads `metadataCache` **embeds**, which include transcluded notes (`![[Some Note]]`). - **Attach to an already-open vault** instead of rewriting `~/Library/Application Support/obsidian/obsidian.json`

  if launch throws afterwards, teardown never runs and the user's global Obsidian config stays clobbered.
- Several CDP page targets exist (devtools, popouts, one per vault). Pick by
  `document.querySelector(".workspace")` **and** `app.vault.getName() === "<vault>"` — title matching alone
  is not enough when multiple vaults are open.
- Reload the plugin between runs so fresh code is tested:
  `app.plugins.disablePlugin(id).then(() => app.plugins.enablePlugin(id))`. Plugin id is
  `@discourse-graph/obsidian`, so command ids look like `@discourse-graph/obsidian:open-node-search`.
- `Runtime.evaluate` bodies are wrapped in a plain function, so `await` at the top level throws —
  return a promise chain instead.
- Playwright is **not** required; ~40 lines of raw CDP over `ws` covers evaluate, `Input.dispatchKeyEvent`,
  `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`, and `Page.captureScreenshot`.
- To distinguish "new tab" from "split", compare a root-leaf count against
  `app.workspace.rootSplit.children.length` — a new tab raises leaves only, a split raises both.
  **`iterateRootLeaves` stops early when the callback returns a truthy value**, so
  `iterateRootLeaves(() => n++)` silently caps the count at 2 (post-increment returns 1 on the
  second call). Use a block body: `iterateRootLeaves(() => { n++; })`.
- **Poll conditions, never sleep.** A 10-line `waitFor(expr)` that evaluates every 25ms took one
  scenario from 24.3s to 1.2s — 8.8s of that was literal `sleep()` calls, and only 0.35s of real
  waiting was ever needed. Naive fixed-sleep CDP is slower than Playwright; polled CDP is a wash.
- Reset workspace state at the start of a scenario, or assertions inherit leftover tabs and splits.
  `getLeaf("tab")` **reuses an empty active leaf** rather than adding one, so with a dirty workspace
  a correct new-tab implementation reads as a failure.
- Close a stray modal with an Escape key event rather than a programmatic `body.click()` — a
  synthetic click on `body` does not hit the modal's background element, so it will not dismiss it.

  September 2026 on Obsidian 1.13.7: the identical scenario went from `body link rendered: false`
  to `true` with those two calls added. The note below still describes the underlying throttling.
- **The Obsidian window must be visible (`document.visibilityState === "visible"`) while scenarios
  run.** When it is covered/minimised/on another Space, Chromium throttles the renderer's timers —
  100 ms → 300–900 ms, and after ~5 min hidden to once per minute — so anything built on
  `setTimeout` (a 500 ms save debounce, a sync debounce, a poll loop *inside* the page) silently
  stalls. It presents as "the feature is broken" (writes land minutes later) with zero errors.
  ENG-2107 lost an hour to this. Check `visibilityState` and a 100 ms timer's real latency before
  believing a timing failure; `electronWindow.setAlwaysOnTop(true)` helps only until focus changes,
  so ask the user to click the window and poll `visibilityState` before firing the scenario.
- The auto-mode classifier blocks quit-and-relaunch as one compound Bash command; run the steps separately.
- **`editor.hasFocus()` is not measurable from CDP.** It reads `false` even for a plain
  `editor.focus()` with no modal involved and `document.hasFocus() === true`; no element holds DOM
  focus at all (`document.activeElement` is the top-level app div). Take a **baseline** measurement
  of the same assertion outside the feature under test before believing a focus failure — ENG-2114
  looked like a focus regression until the baseline failed identically. Assert the observable
  consequence instead (cursor position advanced past the inserted text).
- **Stale `.modal-container` elements poison selectors.** A scenario that times out or throws leaves
  its modal in the DOM, so the next run's `querySelector(".modal-container .modal")` reads the *old*
  modal — producing "footer missing the action" and "modal did not close" failures while the feature
  actually works. Start every scenario with
  `document.querySelectorAll(".modal-container").forEach(el => el.remove())`.
- The plugin **folder** is `discourse-graphs` but the **id** is `@discourse-graph/obsidian`; passing the
  folder name to `disablePlugin`/`enablePlugin` silently no-ops (`loaded: false`, `manifests[folder]`
  undefined). Read the real id from `app.plugins.manifests`, whose `dir` field maps id → folder.

- `detachLeavesOfType("markdown")` followed by `getLeaf(true)` throws **"No tab group found."** —
  detaching the last markdown leaf destroys the tab group the new leaf would go in. Reuse
  `getMostRecentLeaf()` instead of clearing first.
- Obsidian's **Properties** block and the **backlinks-in-document** panel contain **no
  `a.internal-link` anchors**: a link property renders as `div.multi-select-pill-content.internal-link`
  and backlink entries carry no anchors at all. A markdown post processor that queries
  `a.internal-link` therefore cannot leak into either, whatever it scans. Both panels are also
  collapsed/`display:none` by default, so a scenario must expand Properties
  (`.metadata-properties-heading`) and run `backlink:toggle-backlinks-in-document` before asserting.
- **A markdown post processor receives its element DETACHED (`el.isConnected === false`) during a
  normal Reading view render**, but attached and inside `.modal-container` when the plugin calls
  `MarkdownRenderer.render` itself. So `el.closest(".markdown-reading-view")` is null on the real
  path and is the wrong guard; `el.closest(".modal-container")` is the correct tell for "this is our
  own modal preview". Measured with a throwaway `registerMarkdownPostProcessor` probe pushing to a
  `window.__probe` array — a cheap pattern for any question about post processor call context.
- zsh expands `${VAR}` inside `node -e "..."`, silently turning `plugins['${ID}']` into `plugins['']`.
  Write the scenario to a `.mjs` file instead of passing it through `-e`.

### Three behaviour changes you should sign off on

1. **Unquoted dates in frontmatter** now stay strings instead of becoming `Date` (53 fields across 31 notes in your vault). Harmless today — only `nodeTypeId` and `importedFromRid` are ever read, and `body` is never consumed at all — and it makes the plugin agree with Obsidian's own `metadataCache`.
2. **Malformed YAML no longer throws.** `gray-matter` threw; we now return empty frontmatter, matching Obsidian's tolerance. **This is a desktop improvement** — a note with broken YAML previously blew up the import path.
3. `.canvas` embeds upload as `octet-stream` (unchanged from today), not `application/json` as PR #1391 proposed.

I also fixed **two latent bugs in PR #1391** while porting: the `catch` returning `content` instead of `body` (Graphite flagged it; never addressed), and the 4-param replacer that trips `max-params` — which reviewdog fails CI on for added lines.

Yes — four mechanisms, at different layers. I tested the one that actually matters, because the intuitive answer is wrong.

## The trap: a runtime guard cannot save a module-level import

```js
import { save } from "./desktopOnly.js";   // that module does require("fs") at top level
export const run = (isDesktop) => { if (isDesktop) save(...); };   // guard looks safe
```
Simulating mobile (no `fs`), measured:

```
STATIC import  →  THREW AT LOAD -> MOBILE: no fs      ← guard never got to run
DYNAMIC import →  LOADED OK; run(false) -> "skipped"  ← guard works
```

A static import's module body executes at plugin load, before any `Platform.isMobile` check. That's exactly how `gray-matter` and `mime-types` were crashing us.

## The four layers

**1. Build-time — `define` in `compile.ts`.** The expression is substituted before the code ships. This is the right fix for `process.env.NODE_ENV`, since a runtime guard can't help a module-scope read.

**2. Deferred module loading — dynamic `import()`.** esbuild compiles it to `await Promise.resolve().then(() => require_desktopOnly())`, so the module factory runs **only when called**. This is the real per-platform code gate, and it works even in `cjs` format. Verified above.

**3. `window.require()`** — what `nativeJsonFileDialogs.ts` already does. The bundler can't see it, so it's inert until invoked. Same effect as (2) without the ceremony.

**4. Runtime — `Platform` from `obsidian`** (already imported in `keyboardHints.ts`). Confirmed available in obsidian 1.8.7 types:
`isDesktop` · `isMobile` · `isDesktopApp` · `isMobileApp` · `isIosApp` · `isAndroidApp` · `isPhone` · `isTablet` · `isMacOS` · `isWin` · `isLinux` · `isSafari`

For commands specifically, `checkCallback` returning `false` on mobile **hides them from the palette** rather than letting them fail — better than a Notice after the fact.

## One thing you can't do

There's no way to ship separate desktop and mobile bundles — Obsidian loads a single `main.js`, and `isDesktopOnly` is all-or-nothing for the whole plugin. Desktop-only code always *ships* to mobile; you only control whether it *executes*.

## This also validated the guardrail we just installed

My first attempt to build the static-import fixture with the new config **failed outright**:

> The package "fs" wasn't found on the file system but is built into node.

That's `platform: "browser"` + builtins no longer external doing its job: a mobile-breaking dependency now fails the build instead of shipping. I had to pass `--external:fs` to reproduce the old broken behaviour at all.

## So, for the remaining blocker

`execContext.ts`'s `process.env.NODE_ENV` is layer **1** — it's a module-scope read, so `Platform` can't gate it. It needs a `define`. Want me to look at what `IS_DEV` gates before choosing the value? That's the last thing standing between here and "it loads on mobile."
